in_hebrew.name: מריאמן
in_hebrew.meaning: Lady of the Sea, God's Bitterness
in_hebrew.long_meaning: This name is derived from the Hebrew words מרים (mariam) which means ‘bitter’ or ‘rebellious’ and אאל (el) meaning ‘God’. In the context of Mariann, the name translates to ‘Lady of the Sea, God’s Bitterness’.

in_greek.name: Μαριάμνα
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek form of Mariann is Μαριάμνα (Mariamna). The name is derived from the Hebrew name מריאם (Mariam), which means ‘rebellious’ or ‘bitter’, and the Greek prefix α (a), which means ‘Lady’ or ‘Goddess’. Thus, the name translates to ‘Rebelliousness of the Lord’.

in_latin.name: Marianna
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin form of Mariann is Marianna. The name is derived from the Hebrew name Mariam, which means ‘rebellious’ or ‘bitter’, and the Latin suffix -anna, which means ‘little’ or ‘grace’. Thus, the name translates to ‘Little Rebel’.

in_english.name: Mariann
in_english.long_meaning: Mariann is a variation of the Hebrew name Mariam, which means ‘rebellious’ or ‘bitter’. The name is also associated with the Virgin Mary, who is often referred to as the ‘Lady of the Sea’. Thus, Mariann can be interpreted as ‘Lady of the Sea, Rebel’.

Forbearance, the symbolic "bitterness of the sea" embodied in the Mariana name, signifies the inner strength and fortitude required in a deeply spiritual journey.
